title: Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use a wall map of Eastern Africa with a grid of latitudes and longitudes. Facts (to confirm): Ethiopia is the largest country of the region, Tanzania second; the equator crosses Kenya, Uganda and Somalia; Eastern Africa lies east of the Prime Meridian.

skills.key_step: The child names the countries of Eastern Africa and keeps out countries of other regions.

floor.question: Name the country west of Kenya.

representations: a wall map of Eastern Africa
country cards to sort: in or out
steps: Start with Kenya and its neighbours.
Add Rwanda, Burundi, Djibouti and Eritrea.
Check each card against the map.
Leave out countries of other regions.
contexts: a lorry from Mombasa to Kigali

board.do: Draw Kenya and its five neighbours as boxes.
Point at a gap beyond Uganda.
board.say: Which two small countries lie here?

board.do: Add Djibouti and Eritrea in the north.

misconceptions.ask: Which country is in Eastern Africa?
misconceptions.repair: List the ten countries of the region and ask the child to find the country in the list.

misconceptions.ask: Which list has only countries of Eastern Africa?
misconceptions.repair: Ask for the countries on the Horn and ask whether they are east of Africa's middle.

misconceptions.ask: Which one is NOT in Eastern Africa?
misconceptions.repair: Use the compass: Egypt is on the Mediterranean in the north, far from the East coast.

listen_for: No, it is not in the EAC
misconceptions.ask: Is Ethiopia a country of Eastern Africa?
misconceptions.repair: Lay the EAC members on the map in one colour and the rest of Eastern Africa in another.

checks.question: Is Zambia a country of Eastern Africa?
Name two countries of Eastern Africa that do not border Kenya.
checks.answer: any two of: Rwanda, Burundi, Djibouti, Eritrea

skills.key_step: The child describes where each country lies and compares sizes from areas, knowing which countries are landlocked.

floor.prerequisite: Names the countries of Eastern Africa.
floor.question: Name a country of Eastern Africa north of Kenya.

representations: a map with the coast highlighted
steps: Check whether it touches the sea.

board.do: Write Ethiopia 1,100,000, Tanzania 945,000, Kenya 580,000 square km.
Mark the landlocked countries: Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, Ethiopia.

misconceptions.ask: Which country is the largest in Eastern Africa?
misconceptions.repair: Give the areas in square kilometres and ask the child to compare the numbers.

misconceptions.ask: Which country has no sea coast?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which ocean Uganda touches. Then trace where its ships must go to reach the sea.

misconceptions.ask: In which direction does Tanzania lie from Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Stand on Nairobi on a map and say which way Mombasa to Dar es Salaam runs.

misconceptions.ask: Rwanda has more people than Djibouti. Which is bigger in area?
misconceptions.repair: Compare the area column and the population column in a table.

checks.question: Which is the largest country of Eastern Africa?
Is Uganda landlocked?
checks.answer: Yes, it has no sea coast

skills.key_step: The child says latitudes run east to west and measure north or south of the equator, longitudes run north to south and measure east or west of the Prime Meridian.

floor.prerequisite: Names the elements of a map.
floor.question: What is the border round a map called?

representations: a grid drawn on the board
steps: Draw lines parallel to it: latitudes.
Draw the Prime Meridian, 0 degrees longitude, from pole to pole.
Draw lines through the poles: longitudes.

board.do: Draw a circle with a line across the middle.

board.say: What is this line, and what is its number?

board.do: Draw a line from top to bottom.
Ask what this line is called.

misconceptions.ask: Which lines run from east to west on a map?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the equator and say it is a latitude; ask which way it runs.
Ask: which line cuts the earth into north and south? Then give it its name.

listen_for: How far east or west it is
misconceptions.ask: What does the latitude of a place tell you?
misconceptions.repair: Move a finger up and down a latitude line number: the number says north or south.

misconceptions.ask: Nairobi is about 1 degree south. Does that mean it is 1 km from the equator?
misconceptions.repair: Show the degree marks round a globe and measure how far apart two lines are on the scale.

checks.question: What does a latitude measure?
checks.answer: how far a place is north or south of the equator

skills.key_step: The child reads a position as latitude then longitude and says whether a place is north or south of the equator and east or west of the Prime Meridian.

floor.prerequisite: Says what latitudes and longitudes are.
floor.question: Which line is 0 degrees latitude?

representations: a table of towns with positions
a finger walk along the lines
steps: N or S: which side of the equator.
E or W: which side of the Prime Meridian.
contexts: Nairobi about 1 degree S, 37 degrees E
Addis Ababa about 9 degrees N, 38 degrees E

board.say: Is Addis Ababa north or south of the equator?

board.do: Write "north of the equator, east of the Prime Meridian".

misconceptions.ask: Nairobi is at about 1 degree S. Which side of the equator is it?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: what does S stand for? Mark the equator on a sketch and put 1 S below it.

misconceptions.ask: Kampala is at about 32 degrees E. Which side of the Prime Meridian is it?
misconceptions.repair: Read the E on the number and mark it on a sketch to the right of the 0 line.

misconceptions.ask: A place is written 4 N, 36 E. Which number is the latitude?
misconceptions.repair: Say the rule: latitude first (up and down), longitude second (across).

listen_for: North, it is at the top of the map
misconceptions.ask: Dodoma is near the top of a map of Tanzania. Its latitude is 6 degrees S. Is it north or south of the equator?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the equator on the map first and look at which side Dodoma is.

checks.question: A town is at 3 degrees S, 36 degrees E. Is it north or south of the equator?
Is Eastern Africa east or west of the Prime Meridian?
